copies.headline: Adam Is 5-0 And It Isn't Luck
copies.body: The all-play is 49-6. That's 89 percent, first of twelve, and it means Adam hasn't just won five games, he's beaten basically everyone every week. His 154.5 per game leads the league and his season low — 142.9 — would be a career day for most of this room. Luck is only +0.5, so nobody can file a complaint. The draft graded 89 out of 100 on cabin night and the roster still projects 133 a week, best in the league. Week 6 is Noah, who has five career playoff wins and no answer for this.

copies.headline: John Drafted Ninth, Scores Like Second
copies.body: John's draft-night roster graded out at 80, T-9th of 12, which is the kind of number that usually precedes a dress fitting. Instead he's 3-2 with 671.2 points, 134.2 a game, 2nd of 12, and a 37-18 all-play that says the record is undersellinghim by a game. The last three weeks: 121.6, 135.7, 172.7, a 25-8 all-play. Stafford to Nacua, Kyren Williams, and a Bowers-McBride tight end room that shouldn't be legal. Week 6 projects 138 against Logan. Big brother's fine.

copies.headline: Peter's 4-1 Is Mostly Scoreboard Luck
copies.body: Peter is 4-1 with the league's 2nd-fewest points against and plus-1.5 wins over expected, the luckiest mark of the twelve. The all-play says 28-27, exactly middling, T-5th. That's not an insult, it's an audit. The draft was genuinely excellent — 89 of 100, first in the league — and the 163.0 in Week 4 showed the ceiling. Then Week 5 came in at 95.4 with Lamar Jackson and Kyle Monangai both tagged OUT, and the schedule stopped covering. Week 6 projects 109 against Kaleb. Bijan Robinson had better carry it.

copies.headline: Leif Bounces Back With 164 Points
copies.body: Week 4's 82.8 looked like the start of something ugly, then Leif dropped 164.3 and climbed three spots. That's the season in miniature: 131.7 a game, 3rd of 12, an all-play of 33-22 that says the scoring is real and a luck number of exactly 0.0 that says nobody handed him anything. The draft grade was 80, 12th of 12, and the roster projects 114 a week, 10th of 12 — so Josh Allen, McCaffrey and Henry are outrunning the paperwork. Stefon Diggs is OUT. Grant's next, 135 projected.

copies.headline: 1-4 With The Fourth-Best Scoring
copies.body: Christian is the league's cautionary tale about variance: 128.4 a game, 4th of 12, and a 1-4 record to show for it. His all-play is 31-24, his luck sits at -1.8 wins, 12th of 12, and 705 points against is the second-most anyone's absorbed. That's not a team problem, that's a scheduling mugging. The 89 draft grade, T-2nd, still looks right — Jordan Love, CeeDee Lamb, George Kittle, a roster projecting 119 weekly, 3rd of 12. Week 5's 103.1 was the first real stinker. Isaac in Week 6 is winnable. Something has to break eventually.

copies.headline: CJ Is Running On Jonathan Taylor Fumes
copies.body: CJ is 3-2 and the record flatters him by half a win — luck sits at +0.5, and the all-play says 28-27, dead even. The last three weeks tell it straighter: 97.9, 114.6, 112.4, a 14-19 all-play over that stretch, 8th of 12. The 134.7 in Week 2 looks like a fluke now. Jonathan Taylor projects 19 and Jalen Hurts 18, which is fine, but Juwan Johnson at 10 is doing tight end work in a Jake Ferguson economy. Week 6 projects 124 against Mitchell. CJ needs it.

copies.headline: Mitchell Scores Sixth, Sits At 1-4
copies.body: Mitchell is averaging 116.4 a game, sixth of twelve, and has one win to show for it. That's the whole story: 582.2 points for, 644.4 against, luck sitting at -1.3 wins. The all-play says 25-30, so he isn't being robbed outright, but the last three weeks — 149.2, 102.5, 132.9 — are a 54% all-play clip, fifth of twelve. The backfield is the problem, with George Holani's 8 leading an RB room nobody wants. Nico Collins and Matthew Golden both project 16. Week 6 projects 106 against CJ, which won't fix anything on its own.

copies.headline: Grant's 3-2 Is Held Together By Schedule
copies.body: Grant is 3-2 and the numbers are already rolling their eyes. The all-play is 21-34, 38 percent, T-9th of 12 — that's the honest version. He's +1.1 wins over expected, T-2nd-luckiest, and he's allowed 498.4 points, the fewest in the league, which is less a skill than a gift. The last three weeks: 84.4, 104.4, 121.3, a 27 percent all-play, 12th of 12. The 121.3 in Week 5 is a season high, so progress exists. Christian Watson and Zay Flowers project 17 and 16. Week 6 projects 105 against Leif. Sweat it out.

copies.headline: Kaleb's 3-2 Is A Costume
copies.body: The record says 3-2. The all-play says 21-34, 38 percent, and the luck column says plus 1.1 wins — Kaleb is winning games his scores didn't earn. Week 5's 85.7 was the season low and the trend is ugly: 132.8, then 109.6, then that. A 107.7 average sits 10th of 12. The draft was fine — 86, T-4th — but Breece Hall is OUT, Jared Goff projects zero on bye, and the roster projects 112 a week, 11th of 12. Week 6 against Peter projects 103. Costume's slipping.

copies.headline: Scoring Fine, Losing Anyway, Still Stuck
copies.body: Logan is 1-4 with 561.3 points for, 8th of 12, and 736.5 against, the 12th-fewest allowed, which is a polite way of saying everybody shows up for him. Luck sits at -1.5 wins, 11th of 12, so the 27-28 all-play is the honest version: average, not dead. Week 5's 142.3 is the season high and snapped the skid. The problem is forward-looking — this roster projects 107 a week, 12th of 12, and 89 against John in Week 6. The dress is still measuring him.

copies.headline: 2-3 Flatters Isaac's 104 A Game
copies.body: The record says 2-3. Everything underneath says worse: 104.0 a game, 11th of 12 in scoring, an all-play mark of 16-39 that is the honest version of this season. Isaac is up half a win on expectation and has faced the 4th-fewest points against, which is how you survive scoring 89.3 in Week 2. The strange part is the roster projects 118 a week, 4th of 12, even with Saquon Barkley out. Javonte Williams and Malik Nabers are producing. Three straight weeks in the 100s is not what that group should be doing. Week 6 projects 114 against Christian.

copies.headline: The Assassin Can't Find January From Here
copies.body: Noah finally cracked 141.3 in Week 5, which was nice, and it came one week after 110.5 and two after a 79.6 that should be buried at the lake. The problem is the whole body of work: 100.2 a game, 12th of 12, and a 14-41 all-play that says this isn't bad luck, it's bad scoring — luck sits at -0.3, basically fair. A draft-night roster grading 86, T-4th, has produced this. Drake Maye, James Cook III, Garrett Wilson. Week 6 projects 118 against Adam. Postseason assassin, regular-season bystander.

intro: Adam is 5-0 and it isn't a fluke: 154.5 a game, an 89% all-play, and a luck rating of plus-half a point, meaning he's beating the field rather than the schedule. Noah holds down the bottom with 100.2 per game and a 26% all-play, and he doesn't even get to blame the bracket — his luck sits at negative 0.3, which is rounding error. The week's real swing is Leif, up from seventh to fourth on the strength of 131.7 per game, second-best outside Adam and John, finally translating into a 60% all-play. And a note for the two teams tied at 3-2 with matching 1.1 luck: Grant edges Kaleb by two-tenths of a point, 42.7 to 42.5, so eighth and ninth are not a coin flip, they're a photo finish.
